source.title: Measuring Sharpness in Grokking
source.authors: Jack William Miller; P. Gleeson; Charles O'Neill; Thang Bui; N. Levi

record.tranche_reason: The study fits training and validation accuracy curves to measure the relative grokking gap, using a different measurement approach and settings from the original work.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own results relating fitted grokking sharpness to relative grokking gap. It does not report a direct comparison in which the training set is made smaller. Claims in the introduction about other works are not treated as results here.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It deliberately induces delayed generalization, using ϵ=10^-10 and λ near 1 in the linear model and Miller et al.'s spurious-bit concealment in the parity MLP. It then uses these setups to demonstrate a curve-fitting measure of sharpness. Its outcome, how sharpness relates to the relative grokking gap, is a construct no version names. No training-set-size sweep, circuit analysis, regime switch, LLM setting, weight-decay test, cross-run algorithm comparison or optimizer/numerics control is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that both sharpness measures decrease with relative grokking gap in both settings. They give tentative explanations, a complexity-penalty account for the MLP and a chain-rule argument for the linear model, and call for further empirical and theoretical work.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a solvable linear student-teacher framework and a two-layer parity MLP with concealed spurious dimensions, and measures curve shape by error-function fitting rather than reproducing the original transformer experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The settings differ in how grokking is varied: λ in the linear framework and the number of spurious dimensions in the MLP. The fitted sharpness trends differ in their reported log-log slopes across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In both the linear student-teacher model and the concealed-parity MLP, relative and absolute sharpness of the validation jump fall as the relative grokking gap grows. The log-log slopes are −0.21 and −2.97 for the linear model, and −0.49 and −0.55 for the MLP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer grokking delays come with softer, less sudden validation-accuracy transitions.

record.code_released: Relevant code is stated to be in the tiny-gen repository, branch feat/sharpness-and-gap; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: Workshop paper; venue not stated in the text
record.problems: The paper identifies itself as a short workshop paper. Its MLP mechanism explanation is presented as a possible explanation, not empirically validated. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported trends, and numerical trend coefficients are presented in figures.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks; whether delayed generalization arises without deliberate concealment or threshold choices.
All parts: no circuit, memorizing component or progress measure is studied.
All parts: no non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep or weight-norm sweep.
All parts: no weight decay, critical dataset size or ungrokking. The linear model has no regularisation.
All parts: no comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
All parts: no optimizer or floating-point controls.

record.verdict_notes: This is a workshop paper whose contribution is a measurement method; grokking is induced on purpose in both settings. The reader's V1 limits_scope label has been removed, because no row measures what V1 names: the size of the delay against training-set size. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test whether reducing training-set size causes the delay to grow. Its parameter sweeps vary λ in the linear framework and spurious input dimensions in the MLP.
No generalizing circuit or memorizing component is identified or measured, and no continuous circuit-progress measure is tested.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm intervention is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
The study does not test weight decay, a low-norm bias, critical dataset size, or ungrokking. It notes that the linear setting lacks regularisation.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact is tested.

rows.subject: linear student-teacher model (Levi et al., 2023)
rows.size_stated: din, N → ∞ with λ := din / N fixed
rows.operation_detail: Varied λ toward 1 and fitted training and validation accuracy curves.
rows.measure: Relative sharpness Rrel as a function of relative grokking gap m
rows.note: The paper states that sharpness decreases with relative grokking gap; the figure reports the fit. The sweep varies λ, not training-set size directly.
rows.check: Measures relative sharpness against grokking gap in a linear student-teacher model with a regression-to-threshold accuracy, not an algorithmic dataset. Sharpness is not a quantity any version names. λ changes din/N, but the sweep is presented as a way to raise m, not as a dataset-size test of V1. Fit values match Fig. 6.

rows.operation_detail: Varied λ toward 1 and fitted training and validation accuracy curves.

rows.note: The paper states that sharpness decreases with relative grokking gap; the figure reports the fit. The sweep varies λ, not training-set size directly.
rows.check: Same issue as R1, for absolute sharpness. The value exp(-12.27)*x^-2.97 matches Fig. 6.

rows.subject: two-layer MLP trained on parity prediction with concealment
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of spurious input dimensions and fitted training and validation accuracy curves.
rows.measure: Relative sharpness Rrel as a function of relative grokking gap m
rows.note: The paper states that sharpness decreases with relative grokking gap. Input size changes through added spurious dimensions, not through a stated reduction in training-set size.
rows.check: Measures relative sharpness against grokking gap in a parity MLP. Grokking is induced on purpose by adding spurious bits. The sweep varies input dimensionality, not training-set size, and sharpness is a construct outside every version. The value matches Fig. 5.
